chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from the multitude of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from 'Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), in [the case of]

A man who broke his fast deliberately for one day in the month of Ramadan without an excuse, he said: He frees a slave, or he fasts two consecutive months, or he feeds sixty poor people. If he cannot afford that, he gives charity according to his ability.
ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for deliberately breaking a fast in Ramadan without a valid excuse?
ai.summary: In al-Istibsar, Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), establishing the hierarchy of expiation (kaffarah) for deliberate fasting violations, a key topic in Usul al-Fiqh regarding the sequence of obligations. The fallback provision for those unable to perform the primary acts reflects the Shia principle of ease (taysir) and proportional liability, ensuring the expiation remains accessible regardless of economic status.
